title: SWELL: an automated expansion microscope designed to be cheap (X-WOW invention #1), desk-stage design package
description:
SWELL is an open design for an automated expansion microscope, meant to be cheap, that uses the sarcomeres of chicken muscle as a built-in ruler for local expansion. It is X-WOW invention #1, given away free: whoever builds it is welcome to claim the success.

Simulation only. Never built. The project stopped at the desk stage, before its first gate (G0); no gate was passed. This package holds an audit, the design decisions, a bill of materials with mostly estimated prices, optics and photon budgets, and simulation code with synthetic data and tests. No SWELL has been built or tested, and every result in it comes from simulation. Not yet written: the wet-lab protocol, a laboratory's own risk assessments, the mechanical and fluidic design files (no CAD exists) and the instrument software.

This archive is a snapshot of the x-wow.com site repository at the release tag. This version's SWELL package is src/downloads/swell-g0-2026-10-12.zip, SHA-256 6d31f96a739dd1f8cb6fc2d95878db7a64c5b8c2ce3a3a0c587e91065872a95f. It leaves out the original brief, which planned the gel chemistry in a home wet lab (a plan withdrawn on 2026-10-09; the chemistry belongs only in a laboratory with a fume hood), and its README lists the few decisions and rows also left out. It adds a safety sheet (SAFETY.md) that cites a named supplier's safety data sheet for each hazardous reagent in its table, a red-team test by a separate AI agent (failures published as scored), a go/no-go for the label-free pre-image defined and tested in simulation, the prior-art search and the ruler pipeline as a pip-installable tool. The first version, swell-g0-2026-10-09.zip (SHA-256 6003edff0165b19fc3cba11b94afa50ba5c025a49f5443130b167d0c3936d2a6), was withdrawn on 2026-10-10, because it carries the original brief's superseded home-lab plan, and was taken off the site on 2026-10-11.

Licences: text, data and code CC0 1.0; hardware design files CERN-OHL-P v2; the vendored third-party code in src/assets/vendor/ keeps its own licence: three.js (MIT), OpenSeadragon (BSD-3-Clause), PMTiles (BSD-3-Clause) and fflate inside it (MIT); the repository also holds the 32 slide files of the slide game SHRINK (src/assets/slides/, about 276 MB, CC0 1.0); see src/assets/vendor/README.md. The official licence texts (LICENSE, tools/licenses/ and LICENSES/ inside the zip) keep their publishers' own terms, and quotations from others' work stay theirs. The record's licence field says Other (Open) because the parts carry different licences. Excluded from every licence here, whatever the record's licence field says: the X-WOW name and logo, including the logo artwork in src/assets/img/brand/, src/favicon.ico, src/assets/img/og-xwow.png and their copies in docs/. X-WOW is a trade mark, and the X-WOW logo (which includes the name) is a registered UK trade mark, UK00003425680.

MIT holds US patents on expansion microscopy; read the legal notes at https://x-wow.com/swell/credits/#legal before any commercial use. Made by an AI (Claude by Anthropic, used through Claude Code), working from the X-WOW owner's brief and orders.
